How To Apply
How To Apply
If you are interested in being part of our TAMU Physics & Astronomy graduate program and you are ready to apply, you can find important dates and additional details for submitting your application materials below.
Application Dates
Fall Semester
August 1, 2026
Application Opens
Start your application after this date to be considered for fall 2026.
January 10, 2027
Final Application Deadline
Submit your application by this date to guarantee full consideration of your application.
General GRE (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing) and Subject GRE (Physics) test scores are not required for applications. However, any test scores submitted as part of a student’s application package will be considered in the evaluation process.
Apply Now
Please contact admissions@physics.tamu.edu if you need clarification on any of the application requirements.
* If you cannot meet the regular application cycle, the department has some limited flexibility for other admission dates.
Application Information
Applications should be submitted via Texas A&M GraduateCAS before the deadline. When filling out your application, be sure that you are applying to the main Texas A&M campus in College Station. Please note there are separate forms for Astronomy and Physics/Applied Physics, with different requirements.
Application Fee
The application fee for domestic students is $89, while international students pay $114. Limited financial assistance is available for low-income applicants. Please contact admissions@physics.tamu.edu to request assistance.
Required Materials
The Department of Physics & Astronomy requires the following information to be available with your application at the time of the review:
Resume or CV
At least three letters of recommendation.
Application Essay – The Application Essay should be forward looking and explain why you want to pursue graduate studies, why you are applying to our department, and what research topics you would like to study in graduate school.
Personal Statement – The Personal Statement should summarize your previous research experience(s): institution, supervisor, topic, duration, paper(s), or poster(s). You may upload two items, with a two-paged maximum per attachment. Combine into one PDF to upload.
Transcript – for consideration purposes, we will accept unofficial transcripts. However, please note that if you receive and accept an offer, the Office of Admissions will need an official copy of your final transcript. If your official scores and grades do not match any unofficial copies that you submitted. (excluding current courses), your application will be subject to rejection and any offers will be rescinded. Transcripts that are not written in English must be accompanied by a certified translation.
Optional Document: List of publications or statements of research experience (when applicable).
